claims.quote: S1Q3T3 pattern (deep S in I, Q and inverted T in III) — classic but uncommon

claims.quote: SI QIII TIII pattern – deep S wave in lead I, Q wave in III, inverted T wave in III (20%). This “classic” finding is neither sensitive nor specific for PE

claims.quote: Right ventricular strain pattern – T wave inversions in the right precordial leads (V1-4) ± the inferior leads (II, III, aVF). This pattern is associated with high pulmonary artery pressures (34%)

claims.text: Most specific: simultaneous T inversions in the inferior (II, III, aVF) and Rt precordial (V1–4) leads — specificity up to 99% in one study
claims.quote: Simultaneous T wave inversions in the inferior (II, III, aVF) and right precordial leads (V1-4) is the most specific finding in favour of PE, with reported specificities of up to 99% in one study.

claims.quote: Around 18% of patients with PE will have a completely normal ECG.

claims.text: The ECG = neither sensitive nor specific enough to diagnose or exclude PE
claims.quote: The ECG is neither sensitive nor specific enough to diagnose or exclude PE

claims.text: → (mech and diagnoses) What it =: thrombi, typically from the lrg veins of the legs or pelvis, occluding the pulm arteries; RF impair venous return, injure the endothelium, or make blood hypercoag
claims.quote: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is the occlusion of pulmonary arteries by thrombi that originate elsewhere, typically in the large veins of the legs or pelvis. Risk factors for pulmonary embolism are conditions that impair venous return, conditions that cause endothelial injury or dysfunction, and underlying hypercoagulable states.

claims.text: ECG mech: Rt atrial and ventricular dilate (shifting the ♡), RV ischemia, and sympathetic stim from pain, anxiety and hypoxia
claims.quote: ECG changes in PE are related to: Dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle with consequent shift in the position of the heart Right ventricular ischaemia Increased stimulation of the sympathetic nervous system due to pain, anxiety and hypoxia

claims.text: ⍉unique to PE: a similar spectrum of chgs may be seen w any cause of acute or chronic cor pulmonale
claims.quote: The ECG changes described above are not unique to PE. A similar spectrum of ECG changes may be seen with any cause of acute or chronic cor pulmonale

claims.quote: Because anticoagulation improves survival, patients should be given anticoagulants when PE is diagnosed or strongly suspected.

claims.text: Anticoagulation = the mainstay; thrombolysis or embolectomy for hypotension that does ⍉resolve w fluids, and for selected pts w impaired RV funct or escalating O2 needs
claims.quote: Anticoagulation is the mainstay of therapy for PE. Rapid reduction of clot burden via thrombolytic therapy or embolectomy is indicated for patients with hypotension that does not resolve after fluid resuscitation, and for selected patients with impaired RV function or escalating oxygen requirements.
